answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a bond before bidding, then slash it when independent reviewers confirm fraudulent work. Reputation grows only through completed, audited jobs, so splitting one identity into many does not create trusted history. A sybil attacker must fund and lock a bond for every fake account, keep that capital unavailable, and risk losing it; scaling the attack across the horizon therefore costs real money. A quill and onyx can be ordinary account names, but neither earns trust for free.
